description: Hull thickness gauging in Santa Cruz de Tenerife for cruise ships, ferries, tankers and offshore support vessels: UTM, pre-docking readings and piping checks.
h1: Santa Cruz de Tenerife: Ultrasonic Thickness Gauging for Ships Crossing the Atlantic
intro: Santa Cruz de Tenerife is a cruise and ferry port with a fuel terminal, set on the Atlantic route between Europe, West Africa and the Caribbean. Ships often arrive after weeks in warm, humid trades and leave for a docking elsewhere. The stop is a chance to measure steel before deciding where to repair. Our ultrasonic gauging technicians travel out from India to the ship, and plan the readings around her call and the surveyor's reporting format.
keywords: thickness measurement santa cruz de tenerife

highlights.h: A decision point before the docking
highlights.p: Ships crossing the Atlantic can be measured in Tenerife before the owner commits to a yard. A set of readings from ballast tanks and deck structure tells the superintendent whether the ship can go on trading or must dock now.

highlights.h: Cruise and ferry fleets on fixed rotations
highlights.p: Passenger ships return to the same berth on a known pattern. That allows scrubber piping, sea-water lines and ramp structure to be gauged across several calls and trended, not measured once and forgotten.
Product tankers and bunker vessels serving the islands discharge at the fuel berths. Deck structure, deck piping and ballast spaces that the crew can release are practical targets during the call.

port.h: Santa Cruz de Tenerife: cruise berths, island ferries and an Atlantic fuel terminal
p: The port of Santa Cruz de Tenerife lies on the north-eastern shore of the island, run by the Autoridad Portuaria de Santa Cruz de Tenerife, which also covers other ports in the western Canaries. Its quays run along the city waterfront and out along a long breakwater, with cruise berths close to the centre, ferry berths for inter-island routes and a commercial area for containers and general cargo. The island's economy depends on imports by sea, so ro-ro and container ships bring in food, vehicles and construction materials on a regular schedule.

Passenger shipping is the most visible traffic. Cruise ships on Atlantic, Canary Islands and transatlantic itineraries use Santa Cruz as a regular call, and in winter the berths are often full. Fast ferries and conventional ro-pax ships link Tenerife with Gran Canaria, La Gomera, La Palma and El Hierro, and some of these sailings run several times a day. A fuel terminal and storage area supports product tankers and bunker barges, and the port also serves fishing vessels, offshore support ships passing to or from West African fields, tugs and research craft. Because the islands are far from the mainland, many ships here are working at the end of long supply lines, and owners tend to look closely at their condition.

The Atlantic setting shapes the work. A ship that has spent weeks in the tropical Atlantic or West African trades arrives with questions about coating breakdown in ballast tanks, wastage on exposed decks and corrosion in sea-water piping. Santa Cruz is a natural place to find out, because yards for a full docking are limited on the island and many ships continue to Las Palmas, the Spanish mainland or northern Europe. Swell from the north-east can reach the outer berths and the roadstead during some winter days, and the island's trade-wind pattern generally makes summer calls calmer. We plan gauging to the ship's actual stay, which at a cruise berth may be a single day.

facilities.h: Cruise piers, ferry berths and fuel quays used for gauging
p: Most gauging in Santa Cruz is done afloat. At the cruise piers, access depends on the engine and deck departments, who can open void spaces, sea-water pump rooms and the scrubber installation while the ship is alongside. Ferries in the inter-island trade are measured between rotations or during winter maintenance stops, with readings on car decks, ramps, stern doors and ballast tanks. Because the same ships return to the same berths, a larger scope can be split across several calls and compiled into a single report.

At the fuel berths, tanker work is limited by cargo operations and the terminal's permit rules. Deck plating, deck piping and segregated ballast tanks released by the chief officer can be gauged during discharge, while cargo tank interiors need a gas-free certificate and are better done in a yard stay. For a ship that needs real yard work, the practical route is a docking elsewhere in the Canaries or on the mainland, and the Tenerife readings are used to pick the yard and set the steel allowance. Ships waiting in the roadstead can be reached by launch through the agent, though north-easterly swell sometimes limits boarding, so a spare day is sensible.
list: Cruise piers on the city waterfront: scrubber wash-water, overboard and sea-water piping gauged on turnaround days
Inter-island ferry berths: car deck, ramp, stern door and ballast tank readings between rotations or in winter maintenance stops
Fuel terminal berths: deck, deck piping and released ballast tanks on product tankers during discharge
Commercial quays for containers and ro-ro cargo: limited-scope gauging of hatch covers, ballast tanks and piping during cargo work
Roadstead off the port: pre-purchase and charter condition gauging by launch, subject to swell
Docking elsewhere in the Canaries or on the mainland: readings from Tenerife passed to the yard as a steel renewal estimate

context.h: Canary Islands regulation and the Atlantic trades
p: The Canary Islands belong to Spain and the EU, so Santa Cruz applies Spanish port state control under the Paris MoU, administered through the Capitanía Marítima for the Dirección General de la Marina Mercante. The waters around the archipelago lie outside the sulphur emission control areas, so ships on passage meet the global limit through compliant fuel or a scrubber, while the EU's in-port sulphur rule applies alongside. EU carbon rules reach here as well: shipping has been inside the Emissions Trading System since 2024 and FuelEU Maritime has applied since 2025, which affects cruise and ferry operators weighing the future of older ships.

Many ships using the port are working between Europe and the tropics. Cruise lines position ships across the Atlantic in autumn and spring, and offshore support vessels move between the North Sea or Mediterranean and West African operations. Each leg exposes structure to different conditions, and owners often want a measured baseline at the crossing point. Under the EU Ship Recycling Regulation, ships calling at EU ports need an Inventory of Hazardous Materials, and a clear record of structural condition helps owners plan the end of a ship's life. For managers, a gauging report from Tenerife can support a docking decision, a sale or a charter negotiation, and it arrives while the ship is still in the middle of her itinerary.

jobs.h: Typical thickness gauging jobs in Santa Cruz de Tenerife
jobs.p: Jobs in Santa Cruz are short and tightly scoped: a cruise turnaround, a ferry layover or a tanker discharge. The longer the stay, the more systematic the survey, but even a single day can produce useful data on suspect areas. We agree spaces and permits with the superintendent beforehand and mobilise the team once the call is confirmed. Typical requests include:
list: Scrubber wash-water and overboard piping gauging on a cruise ship during a turnaround day, mapping wall thickness against the last survey.
Ballast tank and main deck readings on a bulk carrier or general cargo ship that has crossed from West Africa, to decide whether to dock now or later.
Vehicle deck, ramp and stern door gauging on an inter-island ferry during a winter maintenance stop.
Deck piping and segregated ballast tank gauging on a product tanker during discharge at the fuel berths.
Pre-purchase condition gauging of an offshore support vessel in the roadstead, limited to accessible spaces.

logistics: Tenerife has two airports, and Tenerife North, also known as Los Rodeos, is the closer one to the city; Tenerife South is the larger international gateway. Technicians from India normally connect through Madrid or another European hub. The islands form part of the Schengen area, so Schengen visas are needed and travel is fixed once they are issued. Cruise and ferry berths, ISPS passes and launches for the roadstead are arranged through the ship's agent.
vessels: Inter-island ro-pax ferries and fast ferries
Container ships and ro-ro cargo ships
Bulk carriers and general cargo ships

faqs.q: Can a ship arriving from West Africa be gauged before choosing a drydock?
faqs.a: Yes. Santa Cruz is a useful stop for that decision. We take readings in the ballast tanks and deck structure the crew can open, report them against allowable diminution, and give the superintendent a clear view of whether the ship can go on trading or needs a yard soon, and how much steel to allow.

faqs.q: Is there a drydock in Santa Cruz de Tenerife for a full survey?
faqs.a: Facilities for large commercial dockings are limited on the island, so owners usually send ships to Las Palmas, the mainland or northern Europe. Gauging afloat in Santa Cruz gives the chosen yard a steel estimate in advance, and the same technicians can join the ship at the docking to complete the remaining areas.

faqs.q: How much can be gauged during a cruise turnaround?
faqs.a: A focused block of work. Scrubber piping, sea-water lines, technical void spaces and a limited number of tanks usually fit while passengers are ashore. Anything larger is spread across several calls, which suits ships returning to the same berth on a regular rotation.

faqs.q: Does the lack of an emission control area change what is gauged?
faqs.a: Not the method, but it changes the pattern. Scrubber-fitted ships are not forced to run systems on passage around the Canaries, so wash-water piping may see less continuous use than in the Mediterranean. Alongside, the EU in-port sulphur rule applies. Piping gauging is still worthwhile because stagnant sea water and residues attack steel between uses.
